The real question is which get us faster to a complete feature set

Rewrote this question around your redirect: the options are now ranked by how fast each gets to Paper's full feature set, with what each one costs. A is fastest; it trades away CSS as the stored format.

answers Q-1: C. New CSS-native app, copying over open pencil's MCP server and useful parts. Cleanest model, but editor basics (undo, selection, layers, fonts, export) are rebuilt before Paper features land
discussing Q-2, Q-3, Q-4; next S-2: New CSS-native app decided (D-1); choosing shell, UI framework and first-run behavior

- Req 1: `bun run dev` (scripts/dev.ts) opens a 1440x900 "OpenDraw" window, min 960x600; bounds saved on move, resize and close (electron/main.ts).
- Req 2: top bar, layers, canvas, styles panel with empty states (src/App.tsx, src/panels/).
- Req 3: pan and zoom, 10% to 6400% (src/canvas/Canvas.tsx, viewport.ts).
- Req 4: artboards are DOM elements with their stored CSS (src/canvas/NodeView.tsx); names drawn above.
- Req 5: selection by click, layers panel and Escape.

Progress: edit API with transactions (src/document/store.ts, tree.ts), Paper-style ignoredStyles (styles.ts), undo and redo through the store with menu items that leave cmd+Z to the canvas, autosave with a flush handshake on close and quit plus a sync save on reload (autosave.ts, electron/main.ts), full layers tree. S-2 checks still pass. Next: S-3 acceptance tests.

Reqs 1-7 done.
- Req 1-2: edit API and transactions in src/document/store.ts (Transaction: insertNodes, updateStyles, setText, rename, moveNodes, duplicateNodes, deleteNodes, select), with immutable tree edits that share unchanged nodes (src/document/tree.ts). A failing transaction changes nothing.
- Req 3: Paper-style ignoredStyles in src/document/styles.ts: margin, display other than flex/block/none, offsets on non-absolute nodes, and invalid values.
- Req 4: undo and redo, 200 deep, restoring selection. cmd/ctrl + Z and shift + cmd/ctrl + Z go to the canvas; the Edit menu items show the shortcuts without stealing them, and text fields keep native undo.
- Req 5: everything renders from the store (src/Editor.tsx); the layers panel shows the full tree; the selection outline is measured from the DOM so nested nodes outline correctly.
- Req 6: autosave 500 ms after the last change (src/document/autosave.ts). Closing a window or quitting asks the renderer to flush first; a reload saves synchronously. The main process only saves to files it opened.
- Req 7: IDs are stored in the file and survive reloads.
Checks: `bun run test:engine` (7) plus `bun run test:launch` (8). Not covered: clicking Undo in the native menu, since the test drives the page, not the macOS menu bar.
discussing S-4; next S-5: Building S-4: local MCP server and read tools

Progress: the in-app MCP server runs over stateless Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1, with a token in the discovery file and host/origin checks (electron/mcp/server.ts). The 9 read tools are pure functions over a snapshot of the document plus live canvas layout (shared/mcp/); screenshots and computed styles come from a hidden offscreen render window (electron/mcp/render.ts). The opendraw-mcp stdio bridge is in bin/. A client to bridge to app smoke test works. Dependency correction: only @modelcontextprotocol/server and zod (its schema library) were needed; no hono or valibot. Next: acceptance tests.

Reqs 1-6 done.
- Server: electron/mcp/server.ts (127.0.0.1 only, random port, bearer token, Host and Origin checks, discovery file userData/mcp.json with mode 600).
- Bridge for Claude Code: bin/opendraw-mcp.ts, built to dist-electron/opendraw-mcp.mjs. It follows the app across restarts and answers with a clear not-running error when the app is closed.
- Read tools: shared/mcp/read-tools.ts, jsx.ts, definitions.ts. Screenshots and computed styles come from a hidden render window (electron/mcp/render.ts).
- Bug found by the checks and fixed: scaled screenshots zoomed the editor window too, because Electron shares zoom per origin. The render window now has its own session.
- Checks: tests/mcp.test.ts (bun run test:mcp), 11 of 11 pass. The full suite (bun run test) passes: 8 + 7 + 11.
Limits: find_nodes matches stored CSS, not computed values. I did not run `claude mcp add` against your Claude config; the bridge was tested with a scripted MCP client. To connect Claude Code: claude mcp add opendraw -- node /Users/tulburg/Developer/OpenDraw/dist-electron/opendraw-mcp.mjs

Reqs 1-6 done. - Req 1: the 9 write tools use the same names and arguments as Paper (shared/mcp/definitions.ts). The server forwards each call to the editor window (electron/mcp/server.ts), which runs it in src/mcp/write.ts. - Req 2: HTML import in src/mcp/html.ts. Margins, grid, inline display, tables, scripts and form controls are dropped, and each drop is listed in the response. Supports layer-name, (http, https and data: images) and

- Req 3: create_artboard placement in src/mcp/placement.ts.
- Req 4: every call is one store transaction, so one undo step.
- Req 5: working indicator on the canvas (Canvas.tsx, src/mcp/working.ts), cleared by finish_working_on_nodes or after 30 s.
- Req 6: pageId writes go to that page; the user's page and viewport stay put.
Also changed: artboard content now starts from plain web defaults (16px, black text, browser font) instead of the editor's UI font and theme color. Before this, text in dark mode was light text on a white artboard.
Checks: tests/write.test.ts (bun run test:write), 8 of 8 pass; the full suite passes (8 + 7 + 11 + 8). The landing page matches a plain browser render. The 0.92/255 difference is color profile only (window capture vs sRGB offscreen render); the layout is identical (tests/results/write-*.png).
Limits, worth a follow-up spec: rich text (a  inside a 
) is flattened to plain text and reported; Paper supports some inline formatting. The 30 s auto-clear was not tested end to end. Not covered: the clone tag, local image paths, Paper adjusting sizes when moving into a new parent.
Rich text and in-place text editing

Drafted the next 3, all in discussing for your review:
- S-6 Canvas selection and direct manipulation (new Editor section, SEC-4): select any layer on the canvas (click, double-click to go deeper, cmd+click for deepest, shift and marquee for several), move, reorder flex children by drag, resize, nudge, delete, duplicate, copy and paste. Each gesture is one undo step.
- S-7 Styles panel editing (Editor): the right panel becomes an editor grouped like Paper (layout, size with Fixed/Hug/Fill, position, fill, border, shadow, text), plus a raw CSS view, multi-select with Mixed values, and inline notes for styles the engine drops.
- S-8 Rich text and in-place text editing (Document engine): text layers hold styled spans, so write_html and set_text_content stop flattening formatting, plus double-click to edit text on the canvas with cmd+B/I/U.
Why these three: they turn OpenDraw from something agents draw in into something you can edit by hand, and S-8 closes the main gap left in the MCP write tools. Pages, files and tokens come after.
Order I recommend: S-6, then S-7, then S-8. No open questions: where Paper and open-pencil differ I followed Paper.

discussing S-6; next S-7, S-8: Building S-6: canvas selection and direct manipulation

Reqs 1-8 done.
- Selection rules (click at depth, double-click deeper, cmd/ctrl + click deepest, Escape to the parent): src/canvas/selection.ts.
- Gestures in src/canvas/Canvas.tsx: move for artboards and absolute layers, drag to reorder flex children with an insertion line, 8 resize handles (shift keeps the ratio, alt resizes from the center), arrow nudges, marquee, hover outline, size label.
- Gestures draw through preview overrides (src/canvas/preview.ts) and write to the document once, when they end: one undo step each, and nothing reaches the file mid-gesture.
- Delete, duplicate, copy, cut, paste and select all: src/canvas/commands.ts. Copy also puts JSX on the clipboard as plain text, so a copied layer can be pasted straight into code.
- The layers panel supports multi-select (shift + click) and scrolls to the selection.
Two bugs found by the checks and fixed: double-click had no target because pointer capture retargets it, and fast drags committed the second-to-last position because pointer events outran rendering.
Also changed: tests now wait for the app to exit between suites, which stops one suite attaching to the previous suite's app.
Checks: tests/canvas.test.ts (bun run test:canvas), 7 of 7 pass; the full suite passes (8 + 7 + 11 + 8 + 7). Screenshot: tests/results/canvas-selection.png.
Not covered: reordering several selected layers at once (only the dragged one moves), and dragging layers between parents.
discussing S-7; next S-8: Building S-7: styles panel editing

Reqs 1-7 done.
- Panel: src/panels/StylesPanel.tsx. Groups: Layout, Size (Fixed/Hug/Fill, chosen per layer from its parent), Position (absolute toggle that keeps the layer in place), Fill, Border (all four corner radii), Shadow (editable list), Text (text layers only), and a raw CSS view.
- Fields: src/panels/fields.tsx. Number fields take units and math, step with the arrow keys (shift for 10) and scrub by dragging the label. The color field supports hex/rgb/hsl, alpha, the system picker, an eyedropper, and swatches of the file's colors.
- Value helpers: src/panels/css-values.ts.
- Multi-select shows Mixed; edits apply to every selected layer in one undo step.
- Scrubbing and sliders preview live through the canvas preview layer and record one step when released.
- Dropped styles show an inline note with the reason.
- Fonts: the file's families first, then installed fonts (Local Font Access, loaded when the font field is focused), then common fallbacks.
Also changed: update_styles no longer records an undo step when nothing changes, and Enter in a field no longer commits twice.
Checks: tests/styles.test.ts (bun run test:styles), 5 of 5 pass; the full suite passes (8 + 7 + 11 + 8 + 7 + 5). Screenshot: tests/results/styles-panel.png.
Not covered: the eyedropper and the installed-font list need real user input, so the tests don't drive them. Padding and gap are single fields; per-side values go through the raw CSS view.
